record.what_it_does: Web scraping, search, crawling and browser-interaction API that returns clean Markdown or structured data for AI agents.
record.auth_notes: The REST API takes an API key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Keys are created in the dashboard, and requests without a key work at lower limits. OAuth sign-in is documented only for the hosted MCP server (/v2/mcp-oauth), not for the REST API. A multi-user toolkit would have each user supply their own API key.
record.access_notes: The free plan is $0, needs no credit card and gives 1,000 credits a month, with 10 requests per minute for scrape, map and search. Paid plans (Hobby $19, Standard $99, Growth $399, Scale $749, Enterprise custom) raise the limits. No app review is needed.
record.api_breadth_notes: Documented capabilities are scrape, search, map, crawl, batch scrape, extract, agent, interact/browser sandbox and parse, plus status and cancel endpoints and account usage endpoints. The docs pages I opened list only the scrape, search and interact endpoints explicitly.
record.mcp_notes: Hosted remote servers: https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp (API key or keyless) and https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth (OAuth sign-in). The docs also link a guide to run the server locally.
record.blocker_notes: Self-serve API keys on a free tier. Rate limits on the free plan are low (10 requests per minute), and each user needs their own key.

evidence.quote: Firecrawl is a context API for AI agents. It lets you search the web, scrape pages, and interact with live pages
